entries.coverage: Eligible public and private nonprofit facility repair/restoration/reconstruction/replacement under this StaffordAct provision; not every disaster program or every private home.

reducedShareException.conditions: Facility damaged more than once in preceding10years by same event type and owner failed appropriate mitigation; requires implementing regulations.

incentiveShare.conditions: Recognized state/tribal readiness and resilience investments; statute permits higher shares.

entries.unit: Federal share of actual eligible project cost, not percent of all state damage
entries.budgetUse: Federal cost=actual eligible cost*applicable federal share; nonfederal remainder must follow actual state/local applicant allocation. Do not call remainder exclusively state spending without the allocation rule.
why: Government approves eligible repair costs under the applicable assistance program.
The legal cost-share rule allocates those actual costs to federal and nonfederal payers.
entries.rangeLimit: 75%,25%,85% are distinct statutory cases, not an empirical per-place draw range or universal upper ceiling.
entries.missing: Actual declaration/program share, state/local split, project scope and repair-unit cost evidence; no national universal repair amount invented.

entries.familyFormula: 480000 minus prior-year immediate-relative and specified parole adjustments plus prior-year unused employment numbers; statutory floor226000.
entries.employmentFormula: 140000 plus unused prior-year family-sponsored numbers; not an exact FY2026total without prior-year inputs.
entries.coverage: These are different legal permanent-immigration categories. Immediate relatives under1151(b)(2) are numerically exempt; eligibility/admissibility and country/category constraints still apply.
entries.missing: Actual FY2026 category allocation, carryover counts, diversity-program offsets, eligibility/admissibility, per-country constraints and issued/admitted counts. Admissions observations are not legislative authority.
entries.rangeLimit: 140000/226000/480000/55000 are separate statutory formula components, not interchangeable ends of a policy interval. No universal additional-admissions amount inferred.
